design.objective: Replace the release-management business prototype with a persistent ccb-release module whose windows, applications, workflow linkage, production results, production versions and analytics are driven by real backend APIs, while temporarily retaining only frontend project and R&D master-data selectors.
users: Project developer creating and tracking release applications
Configured workflow assignee reviewing complete release applications
Configuration manager maintaining release windows and deployment results
Authorized reader inspecting production versions and analytics

requirements.statement: ccb-release owns all release-management business tables, rules, state and APIs.
acceptance: No release business state is stored in frontend memory or platform private tables
The module has an independent Maven artifact and focused tests
requirements.source: User selected option A for formal development
counterexample: Application status is mutated only in a Vue repository
Release tables are placed in workflow or system

requirements.statement: The five release views use persistent backend data.
acceptance: Windows, applications, production baseline, production versions and analytics survive page reload and service restart
requirements.source: User requested all functions to be formally developed
counterexample: A view still derives business records from createReleasePrototypeState

requirements.statement: Frontend Mock is limited to project, physical-subsystem and delivery-unit selectors, and submitted snapshots are persisted.
acceptance: Backend stores IDs, codes, names and artifact type snapshots
Historical applications do not change when selector data changes
counterexample: Backend stores only delivery-unit IDs
Mock application status remains in frontend

requirements.statement: Release windows enforce ordered minute-precision dates, immutable project/code, non-overlap, audited edits and the regular-submission switch.
acceptance: Invalid and overlapping windows are rejected
Allowed edits record reason and before/after values
counterexample: A window project can be changed
A closed window can be selected without explanation

requirements.statement: Applications persist one subsystem, at least one unique delivery unit, versions, requirements, explanations and attachments under scenario rules.
acceptance: Backend rejects incomplete or inconsistent snapshots
Emergency and non-emergency fields follow their distinct validation
counterexample: Only frontend validates delivery units
Requirements are stored as comma-separated text

requirements.statement: The server derives regular, urgent, emergency and additional characteristics and fixed workflow codes.
acceptance: Date and history boundaries produce deterministic results
Applicants cannot choose a workflow definition
counterexample: Frontend submits an authoritative version type
Additional is exposed as a selectable version type

requirements.statement: Historical applications produce complete conflict information and state-dependent actions without overwriting old applications.
acceptance: Conflict responses include all business facts except attachments
Cancel, edit-old and create-new follow old-state rules
counterexample: A new application silently replaces an old one
Conflict detail contains only an application number

requirements.statement: Draft, submit, withdraw, cancel, return and resubmit transitions are persistent, optimistic-lock protected and audited.
acceptance: Illegal and stale transitions return explicit conflicts
Every cancellation and result change records a reason
counterexample: Refreshing restores the initial prototype state
Concurrent edits overwrite newer data

requirements.statement: Business submission starts a published workflow by stable code through WorkflowBusinessGateway.
acceptance: A successful submit stores definition version, instance, round and digest
Missing workflow rolls back submission
counterexample: Business code inserts wf_task rows
Frontend fabricates a task ID

requirements.statement: Workflow is the sole source for current node, assignee, opinion, signature, task status and process logs.
acceptance: The detail page shows identical node and round facts in progress and action regions
No approval round is generated from frontend Mock
counterexample: Left progress says configuration review while task context says product review

requirements.statement: Workflow lifecycle events update application state idempotently and only for the active round.
acceptance: Duplicate and stale events do not repeat or corrupt transitions
Approved becomes released and returned/rejected becomes returned
counterexample: Frontend decision success directly becomes the authoritative application state

requirements.statement: Application attachments use the persistent attachment platform, while artifact binaries are not uploaded.
acceptance: Attachment ownership and binding are server validated
Emergency submission enforces a test-report attachment
counterexample: A browser-only file name is treated as persisted
A container image is uploaded as an application attachment

requirements.statement: Production baseline lists the latest released candidate per window, subsystem and delivery unit.
acceptance: Candidate selection uses approval completion order, not version text
All candidate sources are traceable to applications
counterexample: Approval automatically marks deployment success
Lexical version sorting picks the candidate

requirements.statement: Authorized users maintain released, succeeded, failed or not-deployed results with full audit.
acceptance: Failed and not-deployed require reasons
Every change records actor, timestamp and before/after values
counterexample: Deployment result is edited without a reason
Approval result and deployment result share one field

requirements.statement: Production versions are derived from the latest valid successful deployment and recalculate after result changes.
acceptance: Changing success to failure reveals the previous success
Cross-window history remains queryable
counterexample: Released but undeployed artifacts appear as production
A stale frontend pointer remains current

requirements.statement: Emergency applications are assigned to the current production window or nearest future window on release.
acceptance: Assignment is deterministic from completion time
Submission is blocked when no current or future window can receive it
counterexample: Applicant manually chooses an emergency window
Emergency release remains permanently windowless

requirements.statement: Analytics aggregate persistent release data and support consistent filtering and drill-down.
acceptance: Summary counts match detail queries
Subsystem, delivery-unit, requirement, version-type and deployment-result dimensions are supported
counterexample: Charts use a separate fixture
A summary count cannot be reproduced from drill-down

requirements.statement: Protected operations enforce authenticated tenant, RBAC, entity ownership and state on the server.
acceptance: Unauthorized and cross-tenant access is rejected
Project-member validation is explicitly marked deferred while project context is Mock
requirements.source: Repository security rules and confirmed Mock boundary
counterexample: Frontend visibility is the only authorization
The implementation falsely claims formal project data scope

requirements.statement: Menus, permissions, Maven assembly, governance and append-only Flyway schema ship with the module.
acceptance: Fresh schema migrates without manual table creation
Governance and module-boundary checks recognize ccb-release
counterexample: Developers manually create release tables
Published migrations are edited

requirements.statement: Acceptance business records are created only through the real API and workflow path.
acceptance: The full window-to-production flow is reproducible without direct business-table inserts
Cleared business tables render an empty state
requirements.source: User requested real data to validate logic
counterexample: Migration seeds sample applications
Browser acceptance uses createReleasePrototypeState

requirements.statement: The formal release workflow remains usable at desktop and required phone viewports.
acceptance: 1280x800, 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 complete required paths
No page-level horizontal overflow
requirements.source: Current repository H5 contract and prior approval UI requirement
counterexample: Mobile approval requires horizontal page scrolling

invariants: One application belongs to one tenant, project snapshot and physical subsystem snapshot
One delivery unit appears once in an application
Workflow owns task authority and release owns business state
Approval completion and production success are separate facts
Historical applications, workflow rounds and production-result logs are not physically deleted
ccb-release never accesses platform private tables
Frontend Mock never becomes the authoritative source of persisted business state
constraints: Java 17, Spring Boot 3.4.4, MySQL 8.4, Vue 3 and TypeScript
Flyway is append-only and the new migration is V38
Project, subsystem and delivery-unit source modules are not yet available
Continue development on user-selected local branch rokey
Do not depend on biz_form metadata
non_goals: Formal project-management or R&D master-data implementation
External requirement, defect, repository, artifact-repository or AI integration
Semantic version comparison or automatic deployment detection
A second workflow task center or signature implementation

selected_approach.name: Single ccb-release business module with internal domain partitions
selected_approach.reason: Window, application, workflow lifecycle, production result and analytics require cohesive ownership and transactions without moving business state into platform modules.

alternatives.name: Separate Maven modules for each release domain
alternatives.rejected_because: Introduces unnecessary distributed transaction and contract overhead.

alternatives.name: Backend wrapper over frontend prototype state
alternatives.rejected_because: Cannot provide persistence, concurrency control or cross-view consistency.

components.name: window
components.responsibility: Own window dates, availability, switch and change audit

components.name: application
components.responsibility: Own application snapshots, validation, conflicts, lifecycle and rounds

components.name: production
components.responsibility: Own released candidates, deployment results, audit and production-version queries

components.name: release-ui
components.responsibility: Consume formal APIs and render the five responsive views

interfaces.name: WorkflowBusinessGateway
interfaces.contract: Start published workflows by stable code and expose lifecycle integration.

interfaces.name: WorkflowLifecycleConsumer
interfaces.contract: Idempotently apply events for business_type release_application.

interfaces.name: AttachmentGateway
interfaces.contract: Authorize and bind persistent attachments without private-table access.

interfaces.name: Release REST API
interfaces.contract: Persistent windows, applications, production and analytics DTOs.

data_flows.output: Persistent reviewing application and workflow round
Consistent production baseline and current production version

error_handling.condition: Workflow code is missing or unpublished
error_handling.behavior: Submission rolls back and application keeps its previous state

error_handling.condition: Optimistic lock or conflict token is stale
error_handling.recovery: Refresh and repeat an allowed action

error_handling.condition: Workflow event is duplicate or stale
error_handling.behavior: Record or recognize receipt without repeating transition

error_handling.recovery: Upload or select an authorized attachment

error_handling.condition: Emergency application has no receiving window
error_handling.behavior: Allow draft but reject submission before workflow start
error_handling.recovery: Create a current or future window

verification_strategy.signal: Module, schema, governance and all five APIs are present and persistent.
verification_strategy.method: Governance, Maven, Flyway, API and restart tests.

verification_strategy.signal: Snapshots, windows, validation, scenarios, conflicts and states match rules.
verification_strategy.method: Parameterized unit and API integration tests.

verification_strategy.signal: Real workflow and attachment paths drive the business detail without Mock approval facts.
verification_strategy.method: Contract tests, lifecycle tests and browser approval flow.

verification_strategy.signal: Released candidates, deployment results, production versions and analytics share consistent facts.
verification_strategy.method: Transactional integration tests and cross-view browser/API assertions.

verification_strategy.signal: Tenant, RBAC, ownership, state and known project-scope limitation are enforced and disclosed.
API-created records complete the real workflow at desktop and phone sizes.
verification_strategy.method: Isolated-database end-to-end browser acceptance and geometry checks.

assumptions.text: Current platform workflow, attachment and security public contracts remain available.
assumptions.basis: Those capabilities were implemented and verified before this formal module request.
assumptions.falsifier: Compilation or contract tests show the public APIs cannot support release integration.

assumptions.text: Future project and R&D modules can replace selector Mock without changing stored snapshots.
assumptions.falsifier: Future modules require mutable foreign keys instead of immutable business snapshots.

unknowns.question: Final external display formats for application and window codes
unknowns.impact: Display only; internal IDs and relationships are unaffected

decisions.decision: Keep only three frontend selector sources as Mock
decisions.reason: Their source modules are not ready

decisions.decision: Use workflow as the only approval-progress fact
decisions.source: User requested removal of approval Mock

decisions.decision: Separate release approval from deployment result
decisions.reason: Approved artifacts may not be deployed

risks.risk: Formal project membership cannot yet be verified
risks.mitigation: Enforce tenant, RBAC, applicant ownership and entity state; disclose and replace through the future project adapter.

risks.risk: Workflow and business transaction coupling creates partial-start risk
risks.mitigation: Use in-process gateway transaction tests and fail submission atomically.

risks.risk: Prototype and formal DTOs coexist during migration
risks.impact: Two sources of truth can reappear
risks.mitigation: Replace views incrementally but remove business-state Mock before convergence.

risks.risk: Production candidate replacement can obscure prior released versions
risks.mitigation: Preserve source applications and append production-result logs.

approval.evidence: User selected option A, confirmed snapshot persistence, reviewed the landed revision 5 design, and explicitly replied confirmed.
